scope: Corollary 10.1 of the manuscript “Every complex K3 surface is Oka” (preprints/Every-complex-K3-surface-is-Oka-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 042 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c35e20c01dcefe76), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 53. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be a complex K3 surface, R an open Riemann surface, K ⊂ R a compact Runge set, and A = {aj : j ≥ 1} ⊂ R a closed discrete set of distinct points. Let kj ≥ 1 be integers. For every continuous map h : R → S holomorphic near K ∪ A and every ϵ > 0, there is a holomorphic map f : R → S, homotopic to h, satisfying sup z∈K dS(f(z), h(z)) < ϵ, j kj aj f = j kj aj h (j ≥ 1). Finite or empty interpolation sets are also allowed. If each prescribed first derivative is nonzero, f can be chosen to be an immersion.
